text.tspan: Public opinion on common farming practices in the US
Survey responses from about 1,000 US adults in 2025 on their views of common farming practices.
Chickens are kept indoors with little
space per bird
Chickens are bred to grow fast and
struggle to walk and stand
Newborn calves are castrated without
pain relief
Calves are permanently separated from
their mothers at birth
Newborn male chicks are killed in
meat-grinders
Chickens are kept in cages, with less
room than a sheet of paper per bird
Pigs are kept in cages, unable to turn
around for weeks
Pigs are killed in CO₂ gas chambers
Newborn piglets' tails are cut off
without pain relief
